title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 18
paragraphs: While he was thus exhorting them, the horsemen, having surrounded them, were riding toward them as if to destroy them, and were already aiming their missiles as if about to discharge them — indeed, some perhaps did discharge them. Meanwhile the Phokians stood facing them, drawn close together with their ranks closed as tightly as possible on every side. Then the horsemen turned and rode back. I cannot say for certain whether they came to destroy the Phokians at the request of the Thessalians, and then, seeing them take up defense, feared they too might suffer loss and so rode away — as Mardonius had commanded them; or whether, on the other hand, he wanted to test them and see whether they had any warlike spirit. Then, when the horsemen had ridden back, Mardonius sent a herald who spoke to them as follows: “Be of good courage, Phokians, for you have proved yourselves good men, and not as I was informed. Now, therefore, carry on with zeal, for you shall not surpass either myself or the king in rewards.” So far went matters with the Phokians.
